answer.rationale: The write-path p99 degradation began roughly 30-90 minutes after a release went out, a timing pattern matching memory_b1 where rollback cleared a checkout error spike from a bad build without customer impact. Regional failover (memory_b2) was considered since the degradation is confined to the primary region, but failover during peak settlement writes risks dropping or duplicating in-flight transactions, conflicting with the objective of not losing customer writes; rollback is the more contained, reversible action. I verified b1 and b2 to compare risk profiles before committing capacity to one intervention, since only one can be executed this window. Root cause (release vs. load-induced regression) is not fully confirmed, so this remains a probabilistic bet rather than a certainty, and add_capacity/circuit_breaker remain live alternatives for the next window if rollback does not resolve latency.
